To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have identified a tract of C37 residues near the pol III active site that are important for termination, 2) we have isolated C37 mutants with strong phenotypes that cause terminator read-through and 3′ oligo(U) shortening, 3) the C37 mutants have no decrease of transcriptional output relative to control strains

the C-terminal domain of Rpc37 is important for termination of pol III transcription in S. pombe, and that mutations in this domain cause readthrough of termination signals without affecting transcription output.

(1) we have developed S. pombe strains that allow monitoring two termination activities of pol III in vivo, (2) we have isolated many mutants of C37 that have strong phenotypes in the termination activities but no comparable mutants of C53, and (3) we have shown that termination deficiency does not necessarily decrease transcription output
In summary, our research is concerned with
how eukaryotic transcription terminates and the consequences of termination defects on transcription output.
how eukaryotic pol III terminates transcription.
understanding how eukaryotic transcription terminates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
termination is not required for transcription output in S. pombe.
C37 is required for efficient termination and that the C53/C37 complex may have an additional function in pol III recycling.
the C37 subunit is essential for efficient termination of pol III transcription in vivo, but that this function can be bypassed in vivo by mutations in C37 that do not affect transcriptional output.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pol III C53/37 subunit pair is a critical factor in the termination process and that termination deficiency in these mutants is not accompanied by a decrease in transcription output.

the C37 C-terminal domain is essential for pol III transcription termination, that it functions in concert with the C-terminal domains of C11 and C53, and that the C37 domain is a major determinant of termination efficiency.
termination is a dynamic and complex process that can be affected by many factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
termination and recycling of the pol III complex can be decoupled from transcription output in vivo.
termination is not required for pol III recycling in vivo.
termination deficiency in pol III is uncoupled from transcription output and thus termination is likely not rate-limiting in transcription.
